paragraphs: Flock Safety sells license plate readers, video cameras, gunshot detection and response drones to law enforcement agencies, schools, businesses and neighborhoods to help them deter crime, respond to emergencies and investigate safety incidents. Its license plate recognition cameras capture plates and vehicle characteristics such as make, color and body type to generate investigative leads. Responders get an instant alert when a vehicle matches a customer-defined or NCIC hot list. Users include law enforcement agencies, businesses, neighborhoods, apartment complexes, houses of worship and schools.

Beyond plate readers, Flock sells PTZ video cameras for open areas such as parking lots, intersections and parks, and fixed cameras for buildings and city streets. A gunshot and audio detection product verifies gunfire and links each alert with nearby LPR reads and video. Flock DFR, its drone as first responder system, launches a docked drone to the coordinates of a 911 call, LPR hit or gunshot alert and streams live video to officers before they arrive. Solar-powered mobile trailers cover parking lots, retail centers and construction sites, and an optional Alert Response Service puts trained agents on live alerts.

Flock sells on an annual subscription that covers hardware, software, maintenance and support. The company has reduced its recommended default data retention from 30 days to 7 days, which it says applies to new law enforcement customers. Customers control their data and how it is shared, and every search is logged.

quote.text: Flock builds technology that helps communities deter crime, respond to emergencies, and investigate safety incidents.
